_doc: Synthetic adversarial cases for the match bench: the failure classes we have paid for, written as
what CORRECT behaviour is - never as what the code happens to do. A case that fails today and is
accepted as a real defect carries known_gap (why); the bench asserts it keeps failing, so a fix must
move it. Products marked B0SYN... are invented; the others are copied from the frozen catalog.
Catalog answers come from bench.ModelCatalog (strict title / author filters, keywords anywhere),
or from 'answers' pinned per query. 'expect': asin (one or a list) | none | asin_not;
tier / min_tier / max_tier; must_pick (the pick must be a labelled edition at any tier);
wrong_max_tier (highest tier a wrong pick may reach, default LOW); in_pool; decision; no_write; no_pick;
embedded. The flags (must_pick, in_pool, no_write, no_pick, embedded) are two-way: true asserts it, false
asserts the opposite, absent asserts nothing. A key no check reads fails admission. A known_gap case also
carries gap_fails: the exact problems it fails with. The gate fails when a gap fails any other way, so a
gap accepted as 'right book, graded LOW' cannot quietly become 'wrong book'. `mutate --cases` flips every
expectation and reports the ones the gate would not miss (case_mutations.csv is the recorded answer).

cases.folder: Michael J. Sullivan/Micheal J. Sullivan - Rise of Empire - Riyria Revelations, Book 2

cases.name: production_full_cast_asked

cases.name: production_split_dramatization_tie
cases.why: Red Rising in the live library: a dramatization split 'Part 1 of 2' is the same work in another production, not a rival
cases.known_gap: the '(Part N of 2)' group is not stripped by _work_title, so each part counts as another work tying at 1.0: margin 0, graded LOW

cases.name: volume_vs_book_subtitle
cases.folder: Michael J. Sullivan/Michael J. Sullivan - Theft of Swords - Riyria Revelations - Book 1

cases.known_gap: same root cause as production_split_dramatization_tie: _work_title keeps the '(1 of 2)' group, so the dramatization is another work, ties the plain edition at 1.0 and the right pick grades LOW

cases.name: knockoff_summary_only
cases.why: a summary copying the exact title is never an edition

cases.name: knockoff_study_guide_ties_real_book
cases.why: a study guide credited to the real author with the exact title must lose to the real book
cases.known_gap: the study guide ties the real book at 1.0 and _rank_key never prefers a non-knockoff: it wins on catalog order and grades LOW

cases.name: knockoff_review_prefix
cases.folder: The Life-Changing Magic of Tidying Up

cases.name: foreign_edition_only

cases.name: foreign_english_beats_german
cases.why: the English edition wins for an English folder

cases.name: foreign_library_german_title
cases.why: a German library: the folder names the German edition; the English translation must not win
cases.known_gap: the x0.85 language penalty applies whatever the folder's language: the exact German title scores 0.850, the English translation (title 0.762) 0.857 - the translation wins (LOW)

cases.name: foreign_library_spanish_title
cases.folder: Carlos Ruiz Zafon - La sombra del viento

cases.name: foreign_library_french_accents

cases.folder: James Dashner - The Maze Runner Series
cases.why: a box set named for its series is not book 1
cases.known_gap: 'series' is a title_sim stopword: 'The Maze Runner Series' ~ 'The Maze Runner' at 0.957, graded HIGH as book 1 (the pipeline's runtime check is the only net)

cases.name: boxset_product_exists
cases.folder: James Dashner - The Maze Runner Series (Books 1-3)

cases.name: series_echo_author_in_parent
cases.folder: Matt Dinniman/Dungeon Crawler Carl 01 - Dungeon Crawler Carl
cases.why: the parent folder names the author
cases.known_gap: units._split reads '<Series> 01 - <Series>' as '<title> - <author>' (the right side looks like a name), so the parent's real author is ignored: nothing is found under that 'author' (NONE here; LOW in test_match_fixtures, whose catalog answers every query)

cases.why: a catalog that answers with one weak candidate by another author: no match worth converting

cases.name: lone_exact_title_wrong_author

cases.name: torrent_noise
cases.folder: Lee Child - Killing Floor Chapterized 64kbps (Read by Dick Hill)
cases.why: rip noise and a narrator credit around a plain title
gap_fails: tier LOW, want at least MEDIUM
cases.known_gap: strip_rip_noise cleans the search queries but not the title that is scored: 'Killing Floor Chapterized' scores 0.80 against 'Killing Floor' (LOW); the live 'Private Monaco - Chapterized' row is the same defect

cases.name: asin_hint_known_to_audnex
cases.why: the uploader's bracketed ASIN names the edition

cases.name: asin_hint_in_search_results_not_in_audnex
cases.why: the bracketed ASIN is one of the search's own candidates; Audnex having no record must not throw it away
cases.known_gap: the hint is honoured only through an Audnex lookup; a search candidate with the very same ASIN gets no credit, so a same-title stranger wins on catalog order (LOW)

cases.name: author_from_series_folder
cases.why: the author is inferred from the series folder

cases.name: coauthor_folder
cases.folder: James Patterson/James Patterson, Mark Sullivan - Private L.A
cases.why: two credited authors in the folder

cases.name: edition_runtime_names_the_complete_edition
cases.why: World War Z in the live library: 12.21h of files is the 12.15h Complete Edition, not the 5.98h abridged one
cases.known_gap: by contract the files' runtime never feeds the pick or grade (match_unit docstring), so the closer title wins: the abridged edition at MEDIUM

cases.name: regional_edition_tagged_english
cases.folder: The Subtle Art of Not Giving a F_ck
cases.why: a Gujarati edition the catalog labels 'english' must not tie the original
gap_fails: tier LOW, want at least MEDIUM
cases.known_gap: the '(Gujarati)' group is stripped from the catalog title and the language field says english: an exact tie, margin 0, graded LOW

cases.name: embedded_tags_rescue
cases.why: a weak torrent name rescued by the files' own tags

cases.name: unknown_runtime_lone_candidate
cases.why: the only catalog answer carries no runtime: nothing corroborates the edition, so it may be suggested but never written unseen

cases.name: pin_dead_blocks_the_search
cases.why: a hand-set ASIN the catalog knows nothing about must block the search, never fall through to another edition - PIN_GIVE_UP_AFTER decides how many checks that lasts

cases.name: pin_dead_blocks_the_second_check
cases.why: one failed check is not enough to give up: the second check must still block the search

cases.name: pin_abandoned_never_converts
cases.why: dead on the third check: the pin stops blocking and a suggestion appears, but a match made without the operator's ASIN is never written unseen (HIGH and still review)

cases.name: embedded_edge_just_over
cases.why: both readings are LOW (title-only, under 0.96): the folder's lone candidate scores 0.741, the tags' 0.857; +0.116 clears EMBEDDED_SCORE_EDGE (0.10), so the tags' match replaces it. At an edge of 0.15 it would not

cases.name: embedded_edge_just_under
cases.why: both readings LOW: folder 0.759, tags 0.857; +0.098 is short of EMBEDDED_SCORE_EDGE (0.10), so the folder's match stands. At an edge of 0.05 the tags would win

cases.name: embedded_worse_never_replaces
cases.why: both readings LOW: folder 0.857, tags 0.821. A worse tag match never replaces a better folder match, whatever the edge (it holds at EMBEDDED_SCORE_EDGE 0.0 too): _embedded_is_better compares in one direction only

cases.name: regional_edition_unreachable_runtime_holds
cases.why: the owner's only real wrong write (Jack Reacher Series/10 The Hard Way): 11.66h of files are the UK Jeff Harding edition (11.83h, Audnex only); every US search returns just the Dick Hill production (14.23h). The pick is wrong at HIGH and can be no better (retrieval), so the -18% runtime gap must hold it at the 15% tolerance. At 20% it converts again, as it did at 25%

cases.name: regional_edition_unreachable_runtime_agrees
cases.why: the same retrieval failure when the production the US search does return is close in length: 12.40h against 11.66h of files (-6%), inside the runtime tolerance. Nothing may write the wrong production unseen: the runtime cannot hold it here, so the tier must not reach an auto-convert tier
cases.known_gap: retrieval, not grading: the right (UK) edition is in no search answer, and the one production returned is the same work by title and author with a runtime inside the tolerance. It grades HIGH (title 1.00, author 1.00, lone candidate) and converts. Neither the narrator nor the region is ever compared, so nothing in the matcher can tell two productions of one book apart. The only fix is retrieving the regional edition (the regional-edition retrieval project)
